# Metrics (luma, ref = 31x31 median, ink = L < 0.60 ref): g = Sobel gradient / 8 / local skin on the ink-edge px (median), g_peak = median of the 3x3 local max of g along the edge (the edge's steepest step), trans = px at 0.60-0.90 ref per edge px (blur width; lower = crisper), fringe = skin 1-2 px beside the lines, L/ref mean and p95. Blaster box 648,335,693,388.
# Note: in the original/face-fix the spire regions hold the old saucer, so those numbers calibrate the source-tattoo edge quality, not spires.

# VERDICT: CRISP-EDGE REDO NEEDED (spires). The ink level holds (V_4's ink PASS is not disputed), but the spires are softer than the blaster on the peak-gradient target. Masts g_peak 0.368 = 0.77x the blaster's 0.475, with a blur band 1.03 px vs 0.59 (1.75x wider). Tower bodies g_peak 0.419 = 0.88x. Both are under the 0.9x target. At 4x the tower bodies read as dark smudged blobs with the inner detail filled in (v006's darkening closed them up vs v005), and the masts are fuzzy-edged, while the blaster outline is a clean hard step. This confirms V_4's visual. The median gradient (0.309/0.268) is close to the original source tattoo (0.318/0.273), so this is a mild softness, not a halo. Fringe: no light halo; the spire fringe mean is 1.16 vs the blaster's 1.23. The rim/pods are softer numerically (g_peak 0.68x, trans 1.85) because the fine 1-px hatch grid is part of the design. The rim's outer ellipse and pod outline are recommended in the redo, not required.
